summary: VPC endpoint policy preventing S3 model artifact fetches for private deployment
description:
Issue summary: After private deployment onboarding, the customer's model-serving nodes fail to download model artifacts from the S3 bucket during startup. Impact: model pulls time out, endpoints fail health checks, customers observe 503s at control-plane level and the dedicated nodes remain UNREADY. Environment: Private deploy in customer's VPC (us-west-2) using AWS Gateway VPC Endpoint for S3 with a restrictive endpoint policy. Steps to reproduce:
1) Deploy a private agent with model pinning to redwood/open-embed-7b.
2) Agent attempts to fetch s3://finsight-models/prod/open-embed-7b/weights.tar.gz.
3) Agent logs show AccessDenied when calling GetObject; serving runtime retries and eventually fails liveness probe.
Logs / errors: 
- From agent: "ERROR: s3.GetObject AccessDenied: Access Denied
 status code: 403, request id: 3A1A..."
- Control plane: "Model pull failed after 4 retries (403)"
- Customer reports that curl against S3 via VPC endpoint fails unless run from bastion as role user.
Additional context: Customer uses a VPC Endpoint Policy that intends to restrict access to a narrow set of prefixes but uses a deny statement that inadvertently blocks GetObject for the agent role. The private deployment uses instance profile role 'redwood-agent-role' that assumes an STS session; evaluation of the endpoint policy with STS session principal may differ from the console test.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:18 - Maya Patel: Customer opened with AccessDenied on S3 GetObject when agent tries to pull model artifacts. Customer attached endpoint policy and example agent logs. Asked for confirmation if Redwood requires any specific IAM principal format for VPC endpoint acceptance.

2026-03-10 10:04 - Owen Chen (Support): Acknowledged. Asked customer to paste the VPC endpoint policy and the exact ARN of the role the agent uses. Requested a short window to reproduce in our staging environment.

2026-03-10 13:27 - FinSight (Customer) - James Huang: Provided endpoint policy JSON and the role ARN: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-agent-role. Noted that policy was intended to only allow s3:GetObject on prefix 'finsight-models/prod/*'. Attached policy snippet.

2026-03-10 15:45 - Owen Chen (Support): Confirmed receipt. Hypothesis: explicit Deny in endpoint policy for principals outside the account or for operations other than GetObject might be evaluated before the role's allowed action. Escalating to SRE to verify how agent's STS session interacts with endpoint policy evaluation. Added INT-4121.

2026-03-11 08:12 - SRE - Lara Gómez: Reproduced in our staging by applying a similarly restrictive endpoint policy to a test VPC endpoint. Observed the same 403 from the SDK when requests are signed with temporary STS credentials. Noted the endpoint policy included a Condition that compared aws:PrincipalAccount but the STS session came from a different account due to cross-account role chaining. Suggested temporary workaround: allow the role ARN or allow the specific aws:SourceArn for the signed requests.

2026-03-11 11:05 - Owen Chen (Support): Shared reproduction steps with customer and recommended temporary workaround: add an explicit Allow for arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-agent-role to the endpoint policy or narrow Deny conditions to exclude agent role. Requested confirmation if customer can update policy; customer to confirm.

2026-03-11 16:40 - FinSight (Customer) - James Huang: Implemented temporary Allow for the role and reports that agents successfully pulled artifacts and endpoints became Ready. Asked for long-term guidance to avoid broad Allow statements.

2026-03-12 09:22 - Owen Chen (Support): Marked as In Progress — preparing final resolution notes and recommended policy templates. Adding follow-up task for E2E doc updates and onboarding checklist for private deploys.
investigation_notes: Checked agent logs: repeated 403 from S3 GetObject. SDK error shows x-amz-request-id consistent with endpoint path, confirming request reached VPC endpoint.

Applied customer's endpoint policy in staging; reproduced AccessDenied for temporary STS-signed requests. Console IAM policy simulator passed for the role but endpoint policy evaluated separately causing deny.
Confirmed that customer's policy used Deny statements scoped to aws:PrincipalOrgID and aws:PrincipalAccount which excluded the transient principal used by our agent (cross-account role/session).

Observed that S3 gateway endpoint policy evaluation occurs after signature verification but enforces principal and condition matches; cross-account STS tokens can produce different aws:Principal attributes causing policy mismatch.
Checked related control-plane logs: model pull job retried 4 times then aborted; no further errors from serving runtime once artifact fetched.
Looked at similar past tickets (SUP-33210, SUP-61234) — difference: those were DNS/TLS; this is endpoint policy logic and cross-account principal evaluation.
resolution: Root cause: overly restrictive VPC endpoint policy denied s3:GetObject for agent's STS session principal (cross-account/role chaining). Resolution: Customer added an explicit Allow for arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-agent-role in the endpoint policy and removed broad Deny conditions that blocked STS principals. After policy change agents successfully fetched artifacts and endpoints recovered. Remediation steps provided below.
resolution_steps: Short-term workaround: Add an explicit Allow statement for the agent role ARN (arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-agent-role) to the VPC endpoint policy so model pulls are permitted.

Recommended long-term policy: Use a least-privilege allow list that matches the exact role ARNs or aws:SourceIp/SourceVpc conditions instead of broad Deny on aws:PrincipalAccount/org. Example template provided in the related confluence page.

If using cross-account roles or STS chaining, ensure endpoint policy conditions accommodate sts:AssumedRole principals; prefer allowing the role ARN or using aws:SourceVpc/aws:SourceVpce where appropriate.

Onboarding checklist update: include a validation step to run a signed GetObject via the VPC endpoint using agent credentials (we provide a validation script) before cutting traffic to private agents.
Follow-up: INT-4121 created to add an automated policy-checker to the private-deploy onboarding flow to detect endpoint policies that will block STS-signed requests.
